items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to requiring the department of
education to report information regarding counselors, social workers and
psychologists in schools
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1409

SPONSOR: RITCHIE
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to requiring the depart-
ment of education to report information regarding counselors, social
workers and psychologists in schools

 
PURPOSE:

To gather information in order to provide better counseling services to
our students throughout the state by ensuring the state meets the
nationally accepted level of school counselors, school social workers,
and school psychologists per school here.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 adds new subdivision 57 to section 305, which directs the
commissioner of education to submit a report to the governor, temporary
president of the senate, and the speaker of the assembly, and specifies
the data the commissioner must include in such report.  Following the
report, the commissioner must develop a proposal to increase the number
of school counselors, school social workers, and school psychologists to
meet nationally accepted counseling professional to student ratios in
New York State.

Section 2 provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Recent, alarming incidents of school shootings have shone a glaring
spotlight on the connection between school violence and mental illness.
Data shows that one in five students suffers some effects of mental
illness. Students facing stress from personal, academic, social,
emotional, bullying, mental illness and other challenges, who might
otherwise turn to drugs or violence, can benefit from improved access to
mental health services that, in turn, can help to make our schools
safer.

When considering the counseling needs of our students, the American
School Counselor Association recommends a ratio of 1:250 school counse-
lors to students; in New York, the ration is more than twice that, at
1:635 school counselors. Similarly, the School Social Work Association
of America recommends a ratio of 1:250 school social workers to
students, and an even lower ratio of 1:50 where students require more
intensive care. The National Association of School Psychologists recom-
mends a ratio of 1:500-700 school psychologists to students, a ratio
that New York met in the 2009-2010 school year with a ratio of 1:600.
Each of these minimum standards was affirmed in the wake of the tragic
school shooting in Newtown, Connecticut, in 2012.

With the guidance of school counselors, school social workers, and
school psychologists, students stand a greater chance to succeed in
their education and establishing a concrete path to their futures.  This
bill seeks to increase access to mental health services in our schools
by first tracking the number of school counselors, school social work-
ers, and school psychologists who serve students throughout the state,
and directs the state Education Commissioner to develop a plan to
achieve nationally accepted professional-to-student ratios in every
district and region.

The bill also recognizes the state's interest in ensuring safer schools
provides and provides that any additional expense incurred by local
districts in meeting the standards for school counselors, psychologists
and social workers should be reimbursed by the state.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2018: S.7838A - Passed Senate.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Requires the department of education to report information regarding counselors, social workers and psychologists in schools and to implement a plan to increase the school counselor, school social worker and school psychologist to student ratio to nationally accepted standards and provide funding for such.
title: Requires the department of education to report information regarding counselors, social workers and psychologists in schools
